target.title: fix(codex): coalesce in-flight dynamic tool calls
target.body:
## Summary

What changed?
- Add a Codex dynamic-tool in-flight coalescer keyed by `threadId`, `turnId`, `namespace`, `tool`, and canonicalized `arguments`.
- Wire the coalescer into both the main Codex app-server run path and the `/btw` side-question dynamic-tool path.
- Preserve current-main dynamic-tool hooks inside the coalesced call path: `toolCallOrdinal`, `onAgentToolResult`, `onFallbackSelected`, timeout recording, and terminal-outcome suppression.
- Add regression coverage for stable duplicate keys, in-flight-only coalescing, main-run observer hooks, and side-thread duplicate request handling.

## Why

Codex app-server can issue two `item/tool/call` requests with different `callId`s but identical tool name and arguments while the first call is still running. Because OpenClaw previously tracked execution by `callId`, both requests reached the underlying OpenClaw tool execution path. For side-effecting tools, that can duplicate external effects such as sending the same screenshot or message twice.

This change only joins duplicate calls that are still in flight within the same turn. It does not persist a dedupe cache and does not suppress later sequential repeats, so intentional repeated tool use after the first call settles still works.

The coalescing key intentionally excludes `callId`. Codex still receives a response for each RPC request, but duplicate same-turn requests share one OpenClaw-side external execution.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Duplicate Codex app-server dynamic-tool requests in the same thread and turn with different `callId`s but identical tool name and arguments now share the first in-flight execution instead of invoking the underlying OpenClaw tool twice.
- Current rebase tested: Local OpenClaw source checkout on macOS, Node v24.13.1, pnpm v11.2.2, branch `codex-pr-88206-rework`, commit `479cd1bf8500`.
- Upstream Codex contract checked: `../codex` commit `be33f80bc651`; `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs` defines dynamic-tool requests with `thread_id`, `turn_id`, `call_id`, `namespace`, `tool`, and `arguments`; `codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs` sends each request with its own `call_id`; `codex-rs/app-server/src/dynamic_tools.rs` submits `Op::DynamicToolResponse` back using that captured `call_id`.
- Runtime proof retained from the original branch: a local `node --import tsx --input-type=module` probe used the real `createCodexDynamicToolBridge`, `createCodexDynamicToolInFlightCoalescer`, and `handleDynamicToolCallWithTimeout` runtime path with a side-effecting OpenClaw dynamic tool that appends to a temp log file. It concurrently submitted two Codex `item/tool/call`-equivalent requests with `callId=call-send-a` and `callId=call-send-b`, same `threadId`, same `turnId`, same tool, and semantically identical arguments with object keys in different order.

```text
OpenClaw Codex dynamic tool in-flight proof
source branch: codex/dedupe-inflight-dynamic-tools
threadId: proof-thread-2026-05-30
turnId: proof-turn-1
request A callId: call-send-a
request B callId: call-send-b
semantic args equal after canonicalization: yes
underlying tool execute count: 1
side-effect log line count: 1
side-effect log:
2026-05-30T02:43:20.065Z callId=call-send-a text=PowerBI daily report ready target=redacted-feishu-channel
first response: {"contentItems":[{"type":"inputText","text":"sent:PowerBI daily report ready"}],"success":true}
duplicate response: {"contentItems":[{"type":"inputText","text":"sent:PowerBI daily report ready"}],"success":true}
same response object: true
```

- Current rebase regression proof: the new main-run test sends two concurrent `item/tool/call` requests with different `callId`s and reordered arguments, verifies the underlying OpenClaw tool executes once, both request handlers receive the same successful response, and `onAgentToolResult` / `onToolOutcome` still fire with the preserved ordinal hook.
- What was not tested: No live Feishu, PowerBI, or Gateway channel message was sent from this PR branch. The proof covers the narrow same-turn in-flight duplicate dynamic-tool class. It does not close broader duplicate mechanisms in #80040 such as provider-switch or abort-overlap cleanup, trajectory writer scoping, or LCM double-write behavior.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts`
- `pnpm format:check -- extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.dynamic-tools.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.ts`
- `pnpm check:test-types`
- `git diff --check`

## Linked context

Related issue: #80040
